summary: Task 15 cleanly closes the four smoke-test UX findings plus folds in TimezonePicker. AC-T7 zero-touch contract is honored (auth.global.ts / SecurityConfig.java / JobRunrMongoConfig.java untouched), Decision 10 scope-lock is honored (no new localStorage writes), i18n parity is intact (4 new keys in both locales), and cross-file consistency for the new pendingBannerKey writer in settings.vue lines up with the store contract and the useApi 404-interceptor. Findings below are minor/UX polish — none block merge.

suggestions.issue: Inconsistent runtime guard around Intl.supportedValuesOf — defaultTz at line 14-17 was hardened against missing supportedValuesOf in this commit (`typeof Intl.supportedValuesOf === 'function' && ...`), but the refine() at line 31 still calls `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone').includes(v)` unguarded. On the same legacy-Safari path that motivated the defaultTz fix, submit will throw a TypeError before validation can report a friendly error. settings.vue already uses the safe pattern (lines 23-26 build a `timezones` const with the same fallback and then refines against that array).
suggestions.suggestion: Hoist the same `typeof Intl.supportedValuesOf === 'function' ? Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') : [Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone]` into a module-scope `timezones` const (mirroring settings.vue lines 23-26) and refine against `timezones.includes(v)`.
suggestions.benefit: Eliminates the partial-protection asymmetry inside new.vue and matches the helper pattern already shipped in settings.vue and TimezonePicker.vue.

suggestions.issue: Task 15 explicitly requires "Якщо юзер очистив поле — emit empty string" (task file line 144). The current `inputValue` setter only writes to `query.value`; modelValue is never re-emitted when the user clears the input. After Escape/outside-click `closeDropdown()` resets `query = ''` and the input reverts to the original `props.modelValue`. As a result an explicit user-clear does not propagate to v-model. settings.vue's zod refine tolerates empty string (line 80: `v === '' || timezones.includes(v)`), but new.vue's refine (line 31) does not — and either way the documented contract is not met.
suggestions.suggestion: When `inputValue.set('')` is invoked (or on a dedicated 'clear' button), emit `update:modelValue` with `''` so v-model reflects the cleared state. Alternatively, document the deviation in decisions and adjust the task AC.
suggestions.benefit: Aligns the shipped component with the documented task contract; avoids future ambiguity about how a cleared field should behave.

suggestions.issue: `openDropdown()` presets `activeIndex` to the current modelValue's index inside `allTimezones` (line 73-74), but the listbox is `max-h-64 overflow-y-auto`. When the selected zone is far down the list (e.g. Europe/Kyiv ≈ index 250), the highlighted active option is rendered well below the visible portion of the dropdown and the user has to scroll to find it. No `scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest'})` call brings it into view on open.
suggestions.suggestion: After `open.value = true` in openDropdown, in a microtask (`nextTick`) call `document.getElementById(\`${listboxId}-opt-${activeIndex.value}\`)?.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest'})`. Same hook can be reused on ArrowDown/ArrowUp to keep the active row visible during keyboard navigation.
suggestions.benefit: Brings keyboard and pointer UX to parity with native <select> behavior — the user always sees what's highlighted.

suggestions.issue: `v-bind="timezoneAttrs"` on `<TimezonePicker>` spreads vee-validate's field attrs (e.g. `name`, `onBlur`) onto the component's root `<div>` (containerRef) instead of the inner `<input>`. `name="timezone"` on a div is invalid HTML and `onBlur` won't fire on the input the user actually interacts with — only the div-level blur, which doesn't bubble the same way. Submit-time validation still runs through handleSubmit so functional correctness is preserved, but on-blur-validation UX is lost compared to the pre-commit native <select>.
suggestions.suggestion: Either (a) declare the TimezonePicker root as `<input>`-like by using `<input>` as the focusable surface and forwarding `$attrs` only to it via `inheritAttrs: false` + explicit `v-bind="$attrs"` on the inner input, or (b) drop `v-bind="timezoneAttrs"` from both new.vue (line 107) and settings.vue (line 254) since the component already emits `update:modelValue` which is the only attr vee-validate strictly needs.
suggestions.benefit: Removes the invalid-HTML `name` on a div and restores blur-time validation parity with the rest of the form fields (name/description still validate on blur).

suggestions.issue: The explicit GET `/api/v1/projects/{id}` on every mount adds a synchronous roundtrip even for the happy path where the user navigates to settings for an active, fresh project that is already in the store. For a typical mount this is wasted bandwidth and adds ~150ms of perceived latency before the form is wired (handleSubmit/resetForm fire after onMounted resolves).
suggestions.suggestion: Short-circuit the GET when `projectsStore.isLoaded && project.value !== null` — in that branch the store is the source of truth and the GET buys nothing. Only do the explicit GET when the store says the project is missing (covers same-tab back-after-delete + cross-tab stale + foreign-id cases). The current behavior is documented in the comment at line 28-32 but the optimization is straightforward and matches the smoke-test rationale.
suggestions.benefit: Removes a redundant API call on the most common path (user opens settings on the current project) while preserving the new staleness contract for the edge cases the smoke-test surfaced.

suggestions.issue: `handleApiResponseError` invokes `projectsStore.handleStaleCurrent()` (which awaits an internal `fetchAll`) without awaiting and without a `.catch()`. If the follow-up fetchAll rejects (network blip, 401 after session expiry, 5xx) the rejection is unhandled and becomes an unhandledrejection event in the browser. Pre-existing to this task (the interceptor predates task 15) but task 15 doubled the surface area by adding an explicit settings.vue redirect that depends on the interceptor side-effects.
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap as `projectsStore.handleStaleCurrent().catch((err) => console.warn('[useApi] handleStaleCurrent post-404 fetch failed', err))`. Keep fire-and-forget semantics, but make the failure mode auditable instead of silent.
suggestions.benefit: Prevents an invisible unhandledrejection in the stale-current-project path; logs become useful when the user reports 'banner appears then nothing happens'.

suggestions.issue: `new_invalidTimezone_showsValidationError` synthesizes the error path by directly emitting `update:modelValue` from the TimezonePicker component (line 112), which bypasses the actual UI gate the component enforces (only option-click or Enter commits a value). The test is honest about the workaround (lines 96-103 comment) but the assertion ends up validating zod refine() behavior rather than the integration with TimezonePicker. If someone removes the refine() in the future, this test would catch nothing.
suggestions.suggestion: Either keep this as a zod-refine-only test and rename it to `new_invalidTimezone_zodRefineRejects`, or replace it with a TimezonePicker-level spec that asserts the component refuses to emit a value not in `allTimezones`. The latter is the right place for that contract.
suggestions.benefit: Reduces test ambiguity about which layer is being validated; the spec name aligns with the actual coverage.

suggestions.issue: `Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)` for the listbox id has a small collision probability when multiple TimezonePicker instances mount on the same page (e.g. a future multi-form scenario, or even reuse in modals). With 6 base36 chars there's ~1 in 2 billion collision risk — practically fine, but the project already uses `useId()` pattern (Vue 3.5+) in other places.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace `tz-picker-list-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}` with `tz-picker-list-${useId()}`. Drops the (vanishingly small) collision risk and is SSR-deterministic so hydration never sees a mismatch — currently the random suffix is generated independently on server and client.
suggestions.benefit: Eliminates SSR/CSR id-mismatch potential and aligns with the project's existing id-generation pattern.
